messages:
laura: Quick RFC thread — I'm drafting the PRD for Private Deploy (VPC/on-prem) networking acceptance criteria. Need alignment on what we require from customers vs what we must guarantee. Major decision points: egress ownership, supported routing modes (BGP vs static), firewall/ports, MTU/encap, observability hooks, and rollback signals. Ping @miguel @dana @ryan @selene for tradeoffs. :wave:

miguel: +1. my initial take: we should default to customer-managed egress IPs when they require IP whitelisting, but offer an operator-managed NAT option for quick onboarding. BGP is preferred for scale/failover but too heavy for many customers.

laura: Agreed. For the PRD I want explicit acceptance gates. Sketch: 1) Customer provides reachable management plane + test subnet, 2) Routing validated (BFD/BGP optional), 3) Egress scenario validated (ips/nat), 4) ACLs/pass-through ports checked, 5) KMS/audit integration, 6) Traffic shaping/mtu verified, 7) Observability / metrics + alert hooks, 8) Rollback plan + fallbacks. Need concrete tests for each.

dana: For KMS and audit, we need the customer to provide KMS access or a signed attestation if they manage keys. Also clarify retention for flow logs (we can't keep >90 days in hosted console unless they pay).

ryan: Ops note: customers often assume we will handle patch windows and IP rotations. We need to add an explicit clause: any customer-initiated IP rotation must be scheduled and tested in a staging window. Also define emergency change process.

selene: From SRE: add SLOs and error budgets for networking failures affecting inference. Suggested SLO: 99.9% control-plane connectivity during business hours for Private deployments; reduction triggers if prefix withdraws >1m. Also need synthetic test we can run from tenant subnet to verify KV cache warming and TLS handshake times.

laura: Good. We should encode acceptance tests as runnable steps. Draft snippet for the PRD test harness:

```
# PRD: networking acceptance tests (runnable)
- step: control-plane reachability
  command: curl -sS https://mgmt.redwood.example/health || exit 1
- step: egress-ip-check
  plan: outbound to whitelist target (3 endpoints) success >= 3/3
- step: routing-sanity
  plan: bring down primary path, verify failover < 30s
- step: mtu/encap
  plan: send 10MB pkts, verify no fragmentation
- step: observability-hook
  plan: push test trace and ensure it appears in console within 20s
```

miguel: That looks actionable. For routing-sanity we should document supported topologies (single-homed with NAT, active-active via BGP, active-passive). Also list failure modes we will not accept at launch (asymmetric NAT without state sync, unsupported VPN vendors).

laura: Good call. We also need launch/priority guidance: which features are mandatory for GA vs beta. My proposal:
- GA: customer static routes + operator NAT fallback, basic flow logs, primary monitoring hooks, documented rollback.
- Beta: BGP full mesh, KMS bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM attestation, advanced traffic-shaping.

dana: OK but BYOK feels high priority for regulated customers. Maybe mark BYOK as "early enterprise" rather than deep-beta.

ryan: Recommend owners: networking eng -> miguel, SRE -> selene, product -> laura, security/compliance -> dana. Delivery milestone: ready-for-internal-beta in 6 weeks, GA in 14 weeks (contingent on 3 pilot customers).

laura: I'll turn this into a short RFC + PRD section and assign owners. Action items:
- miguel: add supported topologies doc + failure mode list (by EOW)
- selene: synthetic test harness + SLO draft (by Tue)
- dana: BYOK requirements + audit/retention notes (by Fri)
- ryan: operational runbook for emergency rotations + rollout windows (by EOW)

ops-bot: Note: RFC stub created -> https://redwood.internal/rfc/priv-net-2112345678 (auto) :robot_face:

laura: Thanks all — please drop short comments on the RFC stub, I want to lock GA vs beta scope by next Wed. :thumbsup:
